conviction_note: The findings net to about zero (+0.2). I scaled the reaction at abs 8.5 because the 14.6% implied move is far above the name's 3.0% median and the release carries the Q4 guide and probably a first 2027 view; p_up is 46 because 6 of the last 7 prints were sold, beat-and-raise quarters included, and a ServiceNow read-through hangs over the group. A rising 12.3% short interest and an upside-paid skew keep p_up from going lower. The positive findings sum and the slightly negative scaled number disagree in sign because the positives are small capital-return and positioning items, while the reaction history is a measured pattern of selling good prints.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $244.5-245.5M and non-GAAP EPS ~$0.18 (company guide, Q2 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001544522/000154452226000135/q226quarterlyearningsrelea.htm). Consensus is $244.9M per MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/freshworks-nasdaqfrsh-updates-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-08-04/) and ~$245.06M / $0.18 per The Stock Observer (https://www.thestockobserver.com/?p=8967169). The guide and two agreeing estimates make the bar sourced. One MarketBeat EPS figure of $0.15 is an outlier. Non-GAAP operating income guide is $59-61M. FY26 guide is $963.5-966.5M revenue and $222-228M non-GAAP operating income. No sourced consensus exists for the Q4 guide or a 2027 first look.
positioning_check: Short interest 29,267,192 shares, 12.26% of float, days to cover 2.9, report date 2026-10-15, published 2026-10-26. That is up 17.1% from 24,987,927 on 2026-09-30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/FRSH/short-interest/). Shorts were building while the stock made a 52-week high of about $15.45 around Oct 21-23. Options (baseline): 25d skew -9.0 vol points (upside paid), put/call OI 0.12, event-implied move 14.63% against a median own reaction of 3.0%, ATM spread 27% of mid. Spot $14.20 is 8% below the 52-week high, 106% above the 52-week low, -4.7% over 5 days and +3.2% over 20 days. The short is crowded-ish but not at the 18-23% squeeze levels, and the options market leans up.

findings.finding: ServiceNow, the ITSM category leader, reported Q3 on 2026-10-28 after the close. It guided Q4 cRPO growth to 18.5% against roughly 19.8% expected, and the shares fell about 15-18% after hours and premarket, even though revenue beat ($4.11B vs $4.10B) and subscription revenue grew 21%. This is the first large ITSM print since Freshworks last spoke on Aug 4, and it resets sentiment on forward ITSM bookings and guides into FRSH's Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FRSH fell 16.4% when its forward guide disappointed (Feb 2026 print, FY26 guide $952-960M amid a software selloff; https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/02/15/why-freshworks-stock-plummeted-this-week/). It fell 4.3% after its Aug 2026 beat-and-raise.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: FRSH is -4.7% over 5 sessions, which covers the NOW print. If the market had fully transmitted NOW's -17% to an ITSM peer, FRSH's put skew would be bid. Instead the 25d skew is -9 (upside paid) and put/call OI is 0.12. NOW's management blamed company-specific causes (renewals pulled into Q3, on-prem mix, T4C exclusions from backlog), so the transmission to a mid-market vendor is a proxy that FRSH has not confirmed.
findings.independence: The cRPO detail is from a second outlet: https://aiweekly.co/alerts/servicenow-shares-sink-15-after-hours-as-q4-crpo-guide-lands-below-street. Both describe one event. It is a peer proxy, not a Freshworks number.

findings.finding: Freshworks has beaten its revenue guide for seven straight quarters (CFO, Q2 call). Q2 revenue was $237.4M against $233.6M consensus (+1.6%) and above the top of its range. Q3 is guided at $244.5-245.5M with consensus about $245M, so a repeat lands near $248M, roughly +1.2% over the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats are sold: 6 of the last 7 prints closed down. Q2 2026 (revenue +1.6% vs consensus, FY raised) went -4.32%; Q1 2026 (beat) -3.26%; Q3 2025 (beat) -1.90%. Only Apr 2025 was up (+3.0%).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: a beat of the guide is what the street expects from this company, and the reaction history shows the market does not pay for it. The only unpriced part is the size of the beat against a consensus that sits mid-guide.
findings.independence: The Q2 consensus comparison is from MarketBeat: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/freshworks-nasdaqfrsh-updates-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-08-04/. The beat pattern itself comes from the company's own document.

findings.finding: The May 2026 restructuring cut about 500 roles, 11% of the workforce, and was substantially complete by end-Q2. The CFO said Q2's non-GAAP operating income of $55.9M (23.6% margin, 'well above estimates') reflected only the 'partial impact of restructuring savings', so Q3 carries the first full quarter of savings against an operating income guide of $59-61M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's large operating income beat and FY operating income raise ($207-215M to $222-228M) met a -4.32% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely inside the guide: the Aug raise of the FY operating income guide already reflected the savings, and the CFO said leverage is being reinvested in EX sales and AI R&D. Only an operating income print well above $61M would be new.
findings.independence: The 'partial impact' wording is from the Q2 call transcript (https://s21.q4cdn.com/987526491/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Freshworks_Q2_2026_Earnings_Call_Transcript.pdf), a different document from the same company.

findings.finding: The $400M buyback authorized Feb 25, 2026 had about $195.6M left at June 30 after $159M was spent in Q2 alone (18.3M shares). At the Q2 pace the authorization is largely used up by Q3 end, and the company holds $665M cash with no debt. A new or expanded authorization alongside the Q3 print is plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $400M authorization was announced Feb 26, 2026, outside an earnings print, after the Feb -16% reaction. No clean print-day reaction to a buyback is on record.
findings.why_not_priced: Remaining capacity is in the 10-Q but not on any preview found. If a re-authorization were expected, it would show in preview commentary, and none was found. The Q3 share-count guide (266M weighted vs 273M FY) already implies continued buying, so only a new, larger program adds anything.
findings.independence: The authorization is confirmed in the company's own release: https://ir.freshworks.com/files/doc_news/Freshworks-Announces-Board-Authorization-of-400-Million-Share-Repurchase-Program-2026.pdf. The Q2 pace is on the call transcript.

findings.finding: Short interest rose 17.1% in the second half of September to 29.3M shares (12.26% of float, 2.9 days to cover, as of 2026-10-15). Shorts were adding while the stock pushed to a 52-week high, and call open interest dwarfs puts (P/C OI 0.12).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No squeeze has been recorded on this name. The stock has roughly doubled off its 52-week low while short interest climbed.
findings.why_not_priced: Sign is ambiguous. Rising shorts are bears adding into the print, but a 12% short on a print that holds the guide is fuel for a squeeze. The options market already leans up (skew -9), so part of this is in the price.
findings.independence: Skew and P/C OI come from the sealed baseline (yahoo options), a different source from the FINRA-based short register.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call the CEO said AI Agent Studio for Freshservice (launched May, 1,000+ customers on it) was not yet priced and 'the intention is to price in the fall', on a session-based model. That makes the Q3 call the likely venue for a new AI monetization announcement or a first contribution to the outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Freddy AI attach metrics (Copilot on >70% of larger deals, 7,000+ paying AI customers) were in the Q2 release that was sold -4.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a promise on a call, not in any preview or wire summary found. It matters only if the price point or attach is quantified in a way that moves the 2027 growth view.
findings.independence: The current CX AI Agent session pricing ($49 per 100 sessions after 500 free) is per pricingsaas: https://pricingsaas.com/companies/freshworks/diffs/2026W20. That is the CX product, not Freshservice.

findings.finding: Freshworks signed on 2026-10-12 to acquire Torii (Israeli SaaS management, $65M raised, terms undisclosed, described as relatively small), closing in Q4. The Q4 guide may carry small acquired revenue and integration opex, plus the first commentary on the deal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Device42 ($230M, 2024) and FireHydrant were folded in without a print-day reaction on record.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal is public, but its effect on the Q4 operating income guide is not. Tiny in size either way.
findings.independence: The 'relatively small' characterisation is from a Calcalist summary via https://www.beri.net/article/freshworks-torii-acquisition-ai-spend-governance-freshservice-saas-management-customer-continuity.

findings.finding: Atlassian, which competes in ITSM through Jira Service Management, reported two days after Freshworks last spoke (Aug 6). It said Service Collection ARR crossed $1B, cloud grew 31%, and the stock rose about 35%. That is a peer data point of healthy mid-market ITSM demand, against the ServiceNow signal.
findings.why_not_priced: Three months old, so it is in the price. FRSH has since rallied to its 52-week high, partly on the group re-rating. Filed as a small proxy that offsets the ServiceNow read.
findings.independence: A peer proxy. The guidance detail is in Atlassian's own 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001650372/000165037226000031/ex991q4fy26.htm.

findings.finding: Freshworks itself guided Q3 calculated billings growth to about 13% reported (14% cc), below the ~14% revenue growth guide. It said NDR (104% reported, 105% cc) would stay roughly flat in Q3. CX ARR, 41% of total ARR, grows only 3% and is guided to low single digits for FY26. Forward growth is therefore decelerating into the Q4 guide and any 2027 first look, which came with the Q3 print last year (13-14% for 2026).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Feb 2026 print, which carried the first full-year guide (~14% growth), fell 16.38%, the largest reaction in the history. In Nov 2025 the preliminary 2026 color was given on the Q3 call and the stock closed -1.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Billings below revenue is in the company's own guide, but the street anchors on revenue. If the deceleration were priced, consensus for 2027 growth would sit visibly below 14%, and no sourced 2027 consensus was found. EX ARR growing mid-20s on 59% of ARR offsets it: total ARR growth needs EX to hold ~24% for the 2027 view to stay at 13-14%.
findings.independence: Same document as findings 2 and 6 (Q2 call), on a different line (billings/NDR, not revenue beat). The 2026 preliminary color from the Q3 2025 call is per https://ng.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-freshworks-beats-q3-2025-estimates-stock-gains-93CH-2189093 (snippet only, not fetched).

findings.finding: CFO Tyler Sloat had 10,734 shares withheld for tax at $14.72 on 2026-11-01 (code F, RSU vesting) and holds 1,703,156 after. There was no open-market insider selling into the print.
findings.why_not_priced: Routine and mechanical. Filed so the panel sees that the only pre-print insider filing carries no signal.

outside_window.finding: Atlassian reports Q1 FY27 after the close on 2026-11-05. Its Service Collection/JSM commentary is the next ITSM read but lands after FRSH's exit (close 2026-11-04).
The Torii acquisition closes in Q4 2026, after the window. Integration and accretion effects are seen only in later quarters.

baseline_tension: The evidence is mixed. The upside-paid skew (-9) and rising short interest point up, the reaction history (6 of 7 prints sold, beat-and-raise included) and the ServiceNow cRPO shock point down, and I side slightly with the reaction history while keeping p_up near 50 because of the skew and the short.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sells beats): reported-quarter revenue beat finding cut from +0.4 to +0.2.
Lesson 6 (inside what the company already guided): restructuring-savings operating income finding cut from +0.3 to +0.1, because the Aug FY raise already reflected the savings.
Lesson 7 (sign against the upside-paid skew, 12% short and rising): ServiceNow read-through cut from -0.8 to -0.6 and billings/NDR deceleration from -0.6 to -0.5.
Lesson 5 (proxy filed small, not dropped): ServiceNow and Atlassian kept as small peer proxies. Left standing: buyback, positioning, AI pricing, Torii, Form 4; abs_move 8.5 and p_up 46 unchanged.
